title: SecB Fail-Learn Events, Transitions, and Compatibility Rules (WP1 deliverable 6)
description: Binds the five WP1 contracts (Failure Evidence Envelope, Experience Record, Knowledge Artifact, Skill Candidate) and the classification taxonomy into one maturity lattice. Three shapes are defined: (1) event_envelope, the schema-bound event shape for the minimum event families in SECB-FAIL-LEARN-001 section 12; (2) transition_request, the shape asking 'may object X move from state A to state B'; (3) transition_table, the schema for the versioned, data-driven legality table (data/maturity-transition-table.json) that answers that question. This file intentionally does NOT try to express legality via a giant JSON Schema if/then chain across four object types x up to eight states each -- that is unwieldy and untestable in the way this project's own src/control/state-machine.mjs already avoids it (a frozen JS table, not schema conditionals). The legality table is instead a first-class, schema-validated DATA artifact, and semantic-validator.mjs's validateTransitionLegality(objectType, fromState, toState) is the single place that consults it. This mirrors, at the fail-learn layer, the STATE_MACHINES table already implemented for Project/WorkPackage/Session/Evidence objects in src/control/state-machine.mjs -- WP1 does not touch that file; it is a distinct, non-conflicting table for the four new fail-learn object types.

event_type.description: Closed vocabulary, exactly the minimum event families named in section 12.

transition_request.description: Requests permission for object_id (of object_type) to move from from_state to to_state. Legality is resolved by semantic-validator.mjs against data/maturity-transition-table.json -- this schema only bounds the request's own shape.

transition_table.description: Versioned, closed, data-driven legality table. Exactly the four fail-learn object types; every state listed for an object type must be a key with an (possibly empty) array of legal successor states.

$comment: This document is a $defs library, not a single-instance schema. run-validation.mjs compiles it and references transitions.schema.json#/$defs/event_envelope, #/$defs/transition_request, and #/$defs/transition_table as three distinct top-level checks.
